learning_outcomes.text: A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of pneumatics and oleohydraulics.
Ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve pneumatics and oleohydraulics problems using established methods.
Ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out pneumatic and oleohydraulic designs that meet specific requirements.
Ability to design and conduct experiments in pneumatics and oleohydraulics, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competencies in pneumatics and oleohydraulics.
Ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods to solve problems in pneumatics and oleohydraulics.
Ability to combine theory and practice to solve problems in pneumatics and oleohydraulics.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competencies.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the development and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering to meet the required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.

syllabus_topics: Elements of a pneumatic system: compressors, tanks, etc.
Elements of a hydraulic system: pumps, tanks, hydraulic fluids, filters, etc.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment (written test on half of the subject)

assessment_rules: Continuous assessment will consist of a written test on half of the subject, weighted at 50%. The final evaluation for the ordinary session will consist of a written test on the part of the subject not evaluated in continuous assessment, weighted at 50%. Laboratory practices are mandatory; failure to complete them will result in failing the course in the ordinary session. In the extraordinary session, students may take a practical exam; if this exam is failed, even if the theory exam is passed, the student will fail the course.
